title: They Have Come...
text:
They have come.

They invade the blood.

They smell of feathers,

of lack,

of weeping.

But you feed fear

and solitude

like two small animals

lost in the desert.


They have come

to set fire to the age of dream.

A farewell is your life.

But you embrace yourself

like the mad snake of motion

that finds only itself

because there is no one.


You weep beneath the weeping,

you open the chest of your desires

and you are richer than night.


But there is so much solitude

that words kill themselves.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the repeated arrival and the stark final image of words killing themselves.

title: Night Singer
text:
She who died of her blue dress is singing.

She sings imbued with death beneath the sun of her drunkenness.


Inside her song there is a blue dress, there is

a white horse, there is a green heart tattooed

with the echoes of the beatings of her dead

heart.


Exposed to all perdition, she

sings beside a lost girl who is herself:

her good-luck charm. And despite the

green fog on her lips and the gray cold in her

eyes, her voice corrodes the distance that opens between

thirst and the hand that seeks the glass.


She sings.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the blue, white, green, and gray color sequence around the singer.

title: I Called, I Called Like the Blissful Castaway...
text:
I called, I called like the blissful castaway

to the executioner waves

that know the true name

of death.


I have called the wind,

I entrusted to it my desire to be.


But a dead bird

flies toward hopelessness

in the midst of music

when witches and flowers

cut off the hand of mist.

A dead bird called blue.


It is not solitude with wings,

it is the silence of the prisoner,

it is the muteness of birds and wind,

it is the world angry at my laughter

or the guardians of hell

breaking my letters.


I have called, I have called.

I have called toward never.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the repeated calling and the final movement toward never.

title: Where Fear Does Not Tell Tales and Poems...
text:
Where fear does not tell tales and poems, does not form figures of terror and glory.


Gray emptiness is my name, my pronoun.


I know the range of fears and that beginning to sing softly in the ravine that leads back toward the unknown woman I am, my emigrant from herself.


I write against fear. Against the clawed wind that lodges in my breathing.


And when in the morning you fear finding yourself dead (and that there are no more images): the silence of understanding, the silence of mere being, in this the years go by, in this the lovely animal joy went away.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the prose density and the shifting self-address in the source.

title: Poem for the Father
text:
And it was then

that with the dead cold tongue in his mouth

he sang the song they let him sing

in this world of obscene gardens and shadows

that came at the wrong hour to remind him

of songs from his boyhood

when he could not sing the song he wanted to sing

the song they let him sing

except through his absent blue eyes

through his absent mouth

through his absent voice.

Then, from the highest tower of absence

his song resounded in the opacity of what was hidden

in the silent expanse

full of shifting hollows like the words I write.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the repeated allowed song and the final movement into hidden absence.

title: The Motionless Dance
text:
Messengers in the night announced what we did not hear.

A search was made beneath the howl of light.

Someone wanted to stop the advance of the gloved hands

that strangled innocence.


And if they hid in the house of my blood,

how do I not crawl toward the beloved

who dies behind my tenderness?

Why do I not flee

and pursue myself with knives

and delirium myself?


Every instant has been woven of death.

I devour fury like an idiot angel

invaded by weeds

that keep him from remembering the color of the sky.


But they and I know

that the sky has the color of dead childhood.
editorial_note: The invented reflexive force of me deliro is echoed by the deliberately strange delirium myself.

title: The Absent Ones Blow Grayly and the Night Is Dense...
text:
The absent ones blow grayly and the night is dense.

The night has the color of the dead man's eyelids.


I flee all night, I channel the pursuit and the flight, I sing a

song for my ills, black birds over black shrouds.


I scream mentally, I confine myself, I move away from the clenched hand,

I do not want to know anything but this clamor, this rebreathing in the night,

this wandering, this not finding oneself.


All night I make the night.


All night you abandon me slowly as water falls

slowly. All night I write to seek the one who seeks me.


Word by word I write the night.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the night-making repetition and renders resolar as the strange rebreathing.

title: The Light Is Too Great...
text:
The light is too great

for my childhood.

But who will give me the answer never used?

Some word to shelter me from the wind,

some small truth to sit in

and from which to live myself,

some phrase mine alone

that I embrace each night,

in which I recognize myself,

in which I exist myself.


But no. My childhood

understands only the ferocious wind

that hurled me into the cold

when dead bells

announced me.


Only an old melody,

something with golden children, with wings of green skin,

warm, wise as the sea,

that shivers from my blood,

that renews my weariness from other ages.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the self-making phrases live myself and exist myself rather than smoothing them away.

title: This Mania of Knowing Myself an Angel...
text:
This mania of knowing myself an angel,

without age,

without death in which to live myself,

without mercy for my name

or for my bones that weep wandering.


And who does not have a love?

And who does not rejoice among poppies?

And who does not possess a fire, a death,

a fear, something horrible,

even if it were with feathers,

even if it were with smiles?


Sinister delirium to love a shadow.

The shadow does not die.

And my love

only embraces what flows

like lava from hell:

a silent lodge,

ghosts in sweet erection,

priests of foam,

and above all angels,

angels beautiful as knives

that rise in the night

and devastate hope.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the anaphora of who does not and the angelic violence of the close.
